To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
telehealth is used in Asia and there is a lack in high quality research on the effectiveness of telehealth.
telehealth is used for many different health care applications, but that the quality of the evidence base is low and that there is a need for more rigorous evaluation of telehealth in this region.

there is an increasing number of published articles related to telehealth in Asia; most studies were conducted in Japanese and the majority of telehealth applications were store-and-forward, videoconferencing or hybrid; most of the studies were observational and only a few studies included a control group; most of the telehealth applications were related to the medical specialties of cardiology and ophthalmology; and most studies mentioned improved quality or access to health care, but only a few studies assessed cost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to develop and maintain a sustainable telehealth service in a rural community.
the development of an integrated, intelligent and interactive system for telemonitoring of patients with chronic diseases.
the use of information and communication technologies (ICT) to support the management of diabetes mellitus in the UK.

telehealth is an emerging field with great potential in Asia, but that the evidence base is currently weak.
there is no conclusive statement on the use of telemedicine in Asia.
there is no clear evidence to support the use of telemedicine in Asia, but that there is a need for high quality studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
telehealth is an emerging technology in Asia and is used in a wide range of applications.
telehealth has been used in many Asian countries and that the results are generally positive.

the use of telecommunication technology in health services in Asia is still at an early stage, and there is a need to conduct more research on telehealth in the region, particularly in the areas of cost and effectiveness.

the field of telehealth in the Asian countries is still in a very early stage of development, and more research is needed to establish the evidence base for telehealth.
the use of telemedicine is widespread in Asia, but the quality and quantity of the research in this area are not commensurate with its use.
